decisions.reason: The quote 'children with progressive myoclonus epilepsy (PME)' does not establish that seizures are a phenotype of PME. The phrase names the disease but does not describe any phenotypic feature. While the abstract discusses seizure onset and SE frequency, seizures are not explicitly stated as a phenotype of PME in the quoted text or surrounding context that directly establishes this as a phenotypic characterization.

The disease name itself 'progressive myoclonus epilepsy' directly incorporates the phenotype 'myoclonus' as a defining characteristic. The term myoclonus appears in the disease name as an intrinsic descriptor of the disease phenotype.

The quoted passage lists 'neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL; 30)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, these listed diseases are explicitly identified as the etiological underlying causes/associations in this cohort. This clearly establishes the association between NCL and PME.

The quoted passage lists 'Gaucher (5)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that Gaucher disease is associated with/underlying PME in this cohort.

The quoted passage lists 'Niemann-Pick (4)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that Niemann-Pick disease is associated with/underlying PME in this cohort.

The quoted passage lists 'mitochondrial (4)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that mitochondrial disease is associated with/underlying PME in this cohort.

The quoted passage lists 'Lafora (3)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that Lafora disease is associated with/underlying PME in this cohort.

The quoted passage lists 'Krabbe (2)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that Krabbe disease is associated with/underlying PME in this cohort.

The quoted passage lists 'KCNC1 gene mutation (2)' as one of 'The underlying diseases' in patients with PME. In the context of a retrospective study of children with PME, this establishes that mutations in the KCNC1 gene are associated with PME. Although the text mentions 'mutation', the gene KCNC1 itself is reasonably identifiable as the subject of the association.

The quoted passage states that status epilepticus is evaluated 'as a measure of epilepsy control' - that is, it is being measured as an outcome parameter related to disease control, not as a defining phenotype of PME. Status epilepticus (SE) is a complication or manifestation that can occur in patients with PME, but the abstract does not characterize it as a core phenotypic feature of PME itself.
